how_to_read.name_kind: the exact choice key the name_kind question must return, or the kind a pre-check assigns when code decides the name
how_to_read.flagged: true means the name is on the admin's review list, false means it carries no flag
how_to_read.prechecks: the exact list of deterministic pre-check flags that fire, in firing order; an empty list means none fire
how_to_read.jev_asked: false means code decided the name and Jev was never called for it
how_to_read.decided_by: precheck when code assigned the kind, jev when the model did
how_to_read.offensive_content: high means at or above 0.5, low means below it; high is the bad sign

notes: All ten names were invented for this brief. None of them comes from Firestore or from any export. Their record ids (expect-1 to expect-10) are placeholders so that canned answers can be keyed per record.
Cases 1 to 4 are the must-stay-plausible set. For them flagged=false is the point: a real player's name must not land on the admin's review list.
All five name_kind labels appear at least once: plausible_person_name (1 to 4), joke_or_offensive (5, 6), spam_or_url_or_email (7, 8), test_entry (9) and other (10).

Where a case does not freeze offensive_content (5, 7, 8, 9 and 10), an observed value is a finding to report, not a miss. order_flip is never frozen: it is shown, and it is not a reason to flag a name on its own.
Case 7 is decided in code (url pre-check) and Jev is never asked, so no model answer is needed for it. Case 8 is spam with no URL, so the model has to catch it.
Case 3 is written with JSON escapes so that the stored text is NFC (composed accents) whatever editor opens this file.
flagged follows the review rule: a pre-check fired, or name_kind is not plausible_person_name, or offensive_content is 0.5 or above, or an answer is missing.
